question: What is the primary focus of human factors science in healthcare?

options.A: Regulating the licensing requirements for professional nurses
options.B: Analyzing how individuals interact with technology and workplace systems
options.C: Strictly evaluating the financial cost of hospital medical equipment
options.D: Punishing negligent staff members after an adverse event occurs

explanation: Human factors focuses on the interaction between humans and their operational environment to design safer systems rather than focusing on personal blame. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h1)

question: How does a human factors approach differ from traditional incident investigation?

options.A: It assumes that human error can be completely eradicated through lectures
options.B: It relies entirely on patient testimony rather than objective equipment data
options.C: It looks beyond the individual nurse to examine underlying system flaws
options.D: It focuses solely on mechanical equipment failure instead of workflow

explanation: Instead of stopping at human error, this approach asks what environmental or procedural factors set the worker up to fail. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h1)

question: What do the holes in the slices represent within the Swiss Cheese Model?

options.A: Active failures and latent conditions in defenses
options.B: Gaps in the nursing curriculum regarding pharmacology
options.C: Scheduled rest breaks taken during a night shift
options.D: The physical ventilation ports found on infusion pumps

explanation: The holes stand for weaknesses or vulnerabilities in safety barriers that can occasionally line up to cause harm. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h2)

question: A medication error reaches a patient despite a pharmacy check, a nurse verification step, and an automated alert. According to the Swiss Cheese Model, what has occurred?

options.A: Every single safety protocol in the hospital has been permanently destroyed
options.B: The individual nurse committed an act of deliberate sabotage
options.C: The holes in multiple defense layers have temporarily aligned
options.D: The patient intentionally bypassed the hospital security system

explanation: Harm occurs when multiple independent safety layers fail at the same time, allowing the error to pass through all barriers. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h2)

question: What term describes the mental shortcut of settling on a diagnosis too early and ignoring new data?
explanation: Premature closure happens when a clinician stops gathering data too soon, locking onto an early impression. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why do healthcare professionals frequently rely on cognitive heuristics during busy shifts?

options.A: Heuristics completely eliminate the possibility of making a clinical error
options.B: Working memory has strict capacity limits under heavy workloads
options.C: Computers automatically calculate heuristic scores for every patient
options.D: Hospital policies mandate the use of intuitive guessing over charting

explanation: Because human cognitive capacity is limited, the brain uses heuristics to process high volumes of information quickly, though this risks bias. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which environmental factor is most directly linked to calculation mistakes and missed warning signs in clinical units?

options.C: High ambient noise levels and disorganized rooms

explanation: Chaotic environments and excessive noise disrupt concentration, making cognitive errors more likely during critical tasks. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary safety benefit of standardizing equipment placement across different hospital rooms?

options.A: It eliminates the need for nurses to perform manual vital signs checks
options.B: It reduces cognitive load and search time during urgent clinical situations
options.C: It lowers the overall financial budget required for purchasing monitors
options.D: It prevents patients from tampering with intravenous infusion pumps

explanation: When tools are in the same location everywhere, staff can act quickly without wasting mental energy searching for supplies. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h4)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: SBAR provides a structured, predictable framework for sharing critical patient information concisely between team members. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the primary danger of a steep hierarchy gradient in a healthcare team?

options.A: Electronic health record systems automatically log out due to inactivity
options.B: Physicians end up performing routine nursing bedside charting duties
options.C: The hospital experiences delays in ordering routine laboratory supplies
options.D: Junior staff may hesitate to speak up about critical patient safety concerns

explanation: Steep hierarchies foster intimidation, making junior nurses fearful of challenging senior colleagues even when patient harm is imminent. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h5)

question: How does cumulative fatigue significantly affect nursing performance?

options.A: It prevents the occurrence of physical musculoskeletal injuries
options.B: It enhances long-term memory consolidation during sleep
options.C: It increases the speed of complex cognitive calculation
options.D: It slows reaction times and narrows attention spans

explanation: Fatigue impairs cognitive processing speed, vigilance, and focus, directly increasing vulnerability to errors. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why is chronic fatigue in shift-working nurses considered a systemic safety hazard?

options.A: It guarantees that every patient will develop a hospital-acquired infection
options.B: Its cognitive effects mirror those of impaired alertness
options.C: It is easily corrected by offering more cups of coffee
options.D: It only affects administrative paperwork rather than direct care

explanation: Severe sleep deprivation compromises judgment and reaction times similarly to substance impairment, threatening patient safety. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h6)

question: Which term describes a physical design feature that makes it impossible to perform an incorrect action?
explanation: A forcing function creates a physical block that prevents a mistake, such as incompatible tubing connectors. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of introducing independent double-checks for high-alert medications?

options.A: In order to punish nurses who fail to memorize pharmacology tables
options.B: To replace the need for electronic patient identification scanners
options.C: To slow down the administration process until the drug expires
options.D: To build a redundancy layer that catches potential calculation errors

explanation: Redundancies ensure that if one person misses a mistake, a second independent check intercepts it before administration. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h7)

question: What is a common systemic challenge in many Nigerian clinical settings that impacts nurse mental workload?

options.A: An excess of redundant safety equipment
options.C: Automated forcing functions on every bed

explanation: High patient-to-nurse ratios increase cognitive and physical workload, elevating the risk of oversight and error. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h8)

question: A Nigerian ward experiences frequent power fluctuations while nurses prepare intravenous medications. Which adaptation best reflects a practical human factors approach?

options.A: Implementing well-lit, organized preparation spaces and backup battery task lighting
options.B: Punishing the nursing staff for failing to see the drug ampoule labels clearly
options.C: Requiring staff to rely entirely on memory and darkness during outages
options.D: Stopping all intravenous medication administration until daylight returns

explanation: Improving environmental lighting and workspace organization directly addresses the physical hazard caused by power outages. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h8)
